TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence of target engagement with 26.3% objective response rate in injected lesions vs 3.9% in uninjected lesions, demonstrating the oncolytic virus is successfully infecting and lysing tumor cells at the injection site. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: The mechanism appears to be working as evidenced by the dramatic increase in pathological complete response (pCR) rate: 17.1% vs 2.7% (p=0.003), indicating successful tumor cell killing and immune activation. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Mixed results - the primary endpoint RFS missed significance (HR 0.75, p=0.07) but showed a positive trend. However, overall survival was significantly improved (HR 0.54, p=0.05), suggesting clinical benefit. The pCR improvement also supports clinical activity. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses reported beyond the overall population. 5. CONFOUNDERS: The trial appears adequately powered and well-conducted. The primary endpoint miss appears to be due to the conservative significance threshold rather than lack of biological activity, given the strong secondary endpoint results.
